questions.q: In this marketplace's listItem function, what must be true before a listing is recorded?
options: The caller must own the token and the marketplace must already be approved to transfer it
The NFT must already be inside the marketplace contract
The buyer must already be known at listing time
The token must have been minted in the last 24 hours
questions.explain: listItem checks IERC721(nft).ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender and that the marketplace has either a blanket setApprovalForAll or a per-token getApproved -- both before recording anything.

questions.q: Why does buyItem delete the listing before making any external call (NFT transfer or ETH payment)?
options: It doesn't matter when it happens
To save gas on the transaction
This is checks-effects-interactions: clearing state before external calls prevents a reentrant call from seeing a still-active listing
Solidity requires all deletes to happen first syntactically
questions.explain: If the listing were deleted after the external calls, a malicious reentrant call during the NFT transfer or a payment could re-enter buyItem while the listing still looked active, enabling double-spends of the same listing.

questions.q: How does buyItem determine whether a royalty is owed on a sale?
options: It always deducts a fixed 10% regardless of the collection
It calls supportsInterface for the ERC-2981 interface ID on the NFT contract, and only calls royaltyInfo if that returns true
It asks the buyer to self-report the royalty amount
It reads a royalty percentage from the marketplace's own storage, set at deployment
questions.explain: The marketplace checks IERC2981(nft).supportsInterface(type(IERC2981).interfaceId) first, since not every ERC-721 collection implements royalties, and only then calls royaltyInfo to get the receiver and amount.

questions.q: Why does this contract pay out ETH using a low-level .call{value: amount}("") instead of the older .transfer()?
options: .call is required by the Solidity compiler for all payments
.transfer() forwards a fixed 2300 gas stipend that can break payments to some contract wallets (like royalty splitters); .call with an explicit success check is the current recommended pattern
.transfer() sends more gas than .call, which is wasteful
There is no difference between the two
questions.explain: transfer()'s fixed 2300 gas stipend is not always enough for a receiving contract's own logic (e.g. a royalty splitter that does more work on receipt), so call plus a manual success check is the safer, current pattern.

questions.q: What pattern does this marketplace use for handling the NFT between listing and sale, and why?
options: Escrow -- the NFT moves into the marketplace contract the instant it's listed
Lazy minting -- the NFT doesn't exist until it's bought
Approval -- the seller keeps the NFT and only grants the marketplace permission to transfer it later, matching how modern marketplaces like OpenSea's Seaport work
The NFT is destroyed and a new copy is created for the buyer
questions.explain: This capstone deliberately uses the approval pattern rather than escrow, so sellers keep full control of their NFT until the moment a sale actually executes.
